claim_as_stated: RCF audited financial statements disclose $19,225,546 paid to Ren in FY2024 under a related-party administration agreement; $7.51m in 2020
source_date: Audited FS FYE 2024-12-31 and 2020-12-31; Form 990 TY2024 e-filed 2025-11-14
exact_values_found: Audit note (related parties): "Administrative fees paid to Ren for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 were $19,225,546 and $15,543,682"; 2020 audit: $7,514,718 (2019 $7,431,300). Form 990 TY2024 Part VII-B: Renaissance Administration LLC, Administration, $19,225,546; TY2020: $7,514,718.
discrepancies: None material. 2021 audit $10,880,690 vs 990 Part VII-B $10,880,689 ($1 rounding). Audit calls it an "Administrative Services Agreement"; counterparty in 990 is Renaissance Administration LLC.
interpretation_challenge: Audit states RCF and Ren are related parties that are not financially interrelated; RCF board includes two Ren employees. Payment is RCF-specific, not Ren company revenue.

claim_as_stated: The RCF-Ren fee basis was 95% of fundholder fees in 2020-22 and 98% in 2023-24
exact_values_found: 2020/2021/2022 audits: "based on 95% of the value of administrative fee revenue earned by the Foundation from individual fund holder accounts"; 2023 audit: "98% and 95% ... for the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2022, respectively"; 2024 audit: 98% for 2024 and 2023.
discrepancies: Wording: basis is administrative fee revenue from INDIVIDUAL fund holder accounts, not all fundholder/sponsor fees. Amendment date/reason not disclosed.
interpretation_challenge: "Near pass-through" holds only for individual-account admin-fee revenue; other RCF revenue (e.g., non-individual accounts) is outside the formula.

claim_as_stated: Edward Jones Charitable Gift Fund is sponsored/administered by Renaissance Charitable Foundation; donor portal is edwardjones.donorfirstx.com; min $10,000 initial, $250 grant
source_date: Portal live 2026-11-14; EJ brochure ANG-13116H (c)2026, exp 31 Mar 2027
exact_values_found: Portal: "Renaissance Charitable Foundation has partnered with Edward Jones to manage and administer your Edward Jones Charitable Gift Fund account"; footer "DFX powered by Ren". EJ brochure: "minimum initial contribution ... is $10,000" (cash/marketable securities); "The minimum grant size is $250."
discrepancies: EJ brochure does not name RCF; it refers only to "a third-party administrator". Sponsor status inferred from portal plus RCF program list (renaissancecharitable.org/llms.txt lists "EJ DAF") and RCF FAQ self-description as sponsoring charity.
interpretation_challenge: Portal wording is "manage and administer", not "sponsor"; sponsor role relies on RCF materials, not an Edward Jones legal document.

claim_as_stated: Ren supplies technology and operational support for RCF programs (RCF FAQ); historical circular names RenPSG as accounting/administrative service provider
exact_values_found: FAQ: "Ren is the technology and services provider that powers Renaissance Charitable's programs. Ren supplies the institutional-grade platform, administrative infrastructure, and operational support". Circular: "The Foundation has retained RenPSG of Indianapolis, Indiana to perform certain accounting and administrative functions for the Foundation."
discrepancies: Claim paraphrase drops "administrative infrastructure"; circular is the RCF Giving Fund circular, not Edward Jones-specific.
interpretation_challenge: Sources establish Ren as administrator as well as technology vendor (audits also say "administration services"). Do not frame Ren as technology-only.

claim_as_stated: A 2021/2022 Ren adviser guide states RCF supported more than $2.9 billion in DAF assets for Edward Jones and its clients
source_date: Unknown (search index described a March 2021 guide; URL path 2022/03)
exact_values_found: Primary PDF returns 404; web.archive.org not reachable from this environment. Only a search-engine summary paraphrased "supports more than $2.9 billion in donor-advised fund assets for Edward Jones and its clients"; a second exact-phrase search returned no match.
discrepancies: Date unresolved (2021 vs 2022). Subject of "supports" (Ren/the firm vs RCF) not verified.
interpretation_challenge: Even if accurate, it is a vendor marketing figure from about 2021-22, not current EJ program assets or audited data.

claim_as_stated: Foundation Source acquired Vennfi (Charityvest's technology) in October 2024 and TIFIN's Giving Place in 2025
exact_values_found: "announced it acquired Vennfi, the financial technology company powering Charityvest" (Oct 17, 2024). "acquired Giving Place, a software platform for family office giving programs and private foundations, from Give, a TIFIN Company" (Apr 30, 2025). Charityvest 990 TY2024 Sch O: "During 2024, Vennfi, inc. was acquired by Foundation Source".
discrepancies: None.
interpretation_challenge: Giving Place is private-foundation/family-office software, not TIFIN Give's DAF platform; it is not evidence of DAF-platform consolidation.

claim_as_stated: TIAA Wealth Management launched a DAF on/around Sept 28 2026 sponsored by Charityvest and powered by Foundation Source technology
exact_values_found: "Through a partnership with Charityvest, a 501(c)(3) public charity powered by Foundation Source"; disclosure: "donor-advised funds sponsored by Charityvest"; footnote: "Charityvest operates on Foundation Source's enterprise-grade ... with DAF sponsor, Charityvest, Inc."; TIAA-CREF Individual & Institutional Services, LLC "receives advisory fees for providing investment advice to donor-advised funds sponsored by Charityvest".
discrepancies: None.
interpretation_challenge: Release is an announcement, not evidence of assets or accounts. TIAA affiliate earns advisory fees on DAF assets (adviser incentive).

claim_as_stated: Charityvest board includes Stephen Kump, Foundation Source DAF Technology President, while Foundation Source is its fee-paid tech/admin provider
exact_values_found: 990 Part VII: STEPHEN KUMP, PRESIDENT, 40 hrs, director and officer. Sch O: Charityvest "DELEGATED CERTAIN MANAGEMENT DUTIES TO VENNFI"; agreement "maintained in place with Foundation Source"; Kump "IS COMPENSATED BY FOUNDATION SOURCE"; 2024 comp from Vennfi $163,944. Part IX line 24a "PLATFORM FEE" $653,137 (payee not named). FS team page: "President, DAF Division"; press release: "President of DAFs at Foundation Source".
discrepancies: Title: primary sources say "President, DAF Division"/"President of DAFs", not "DAF Technology President" (repo cites a Charityvest roster not checked here). Kump is Charityvest President (officer), not only a board member. Payee of fees not named in 990.
contradictory_evidence: 990 Part VII-B lists 0 independent contractors >$100,000, although a $653,137 platform fee was paid; if FS were the payee it would normally be listed. Inconsistency unresolved.
interpretation_challenge: Conflict is stronger than stated (vendor-paid executive runs the charity), but "fee-paid" to FS is inferred, not shown.

claim_as_stated: Charityvest reported 2025 contributions ~$265.5M, grants $119.2M, 48,744 grants, $224.6M assets
exact_values_found: Annual report: "Contributions: 13,956 transactions totaling $265.5M (167%)"; "Grants: 48,744 transactions totaling $119.2M (128%)"; "Assets under management: $224.6M (84%)". Press release rounds to $265 million, up from $99.2M (2024); grants up from $52.2M. Arithmetic: 265.5/99.2-1=167.6%; 119.2/52.2-1=128.4%.
discrepancies: Claim says "assets"; source says "assets under management". Company-reported, unaudited; 2025 Form 990 not yet available.
contradictory_evidence: Company 2024 baselines differ from Charityvest Form 990 TY2024: 990 contributions $111,895,516 vs company $99.2M; 990 net assets end-2024 $103,172,624 vs implied 2024 AUM $122.1M (224.6/1.84). Definitions differ.
interpretation_challenge: Use as company-reported KPIs; do not mix with 990 figures in YoY calculations.

claim_as_stated: Daffy Charitable Fund (EIN 86-3177440) FY2024 Form 990: net assets $334.19M; contributions $194.04M; expenses $40.20M
exact_values_found: Line 8 contributions $194,043,157; line 18 total expenses $40,201,570; line 22 net assets $334,188,937; total revenue $197,184,036.

contradictory_evidence: None found. Daffy press release states $334 million at end of 2024, consistent.

claim_as_stated: Daffy reported $2B charitable assets in Sept 2026, up from $720M in 2025 (company-reported, unaudited)
exact_values_found: "surpassed $2 billion in charitable assets"; "Daffy entered 2026 with more than $720 million in charitable assets, up from $334 million at the end of 2024"; "All Daffy figures are based on initial unaudited results from 1/1/2026 to 8/31/2026." Ratio 2000/720=2.78x.
discrepancies: Release dated Sept 30, 2026. "$720M in 2025" means year-end 2025.
interpretation_challenge: Growth is driven by public and private stock gifts ($600M+ private/restricted); private-stock valuations make the $2B figure valuation-sensitive.

claim_as_stated: Chariot's October 2026 nonprofit terms specify a default 2.9% DAFpay donation fee absent other platform agreements
exact_values_found: "You will pay the applicable DAFpay Fees per your agreements with any Fundraising Platforms, or if no such agreements exist, you will pay 2.9% (rounded to the nearest whole dollar) of the amount of any donation made through DAFpay".
discrepancies: None.
interpretation_challenge: Default only; Chariot may reduce fees and a Chariot Subscription can remove per-transaction DAFpay fees. Fee is paid by nonprofit, not donor.

claim_as_stated: AEF July 2025 press release claimed SOC 2 Type II for its Ren-powered platform; April 2026 language said Type I
exact_values_found: July 2025: "the company holds a SOC 2 Type 2 certification". April 2026: "Ren holds a SOC 2 Type 1 certification".
discrepancies: Attribution: both statements are in the "About Ren" boilerplate and describe Ren the company. AEF does not claim SOC 2 for "its Ren-powered platform". Source wording is Type 2/Type 1, not II/I.
contradictory_evidence: Sequence (Type 2 then Type 1) is inconsistent; no SOC report seen.
interpretation_challenge: SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a certification; neither statement gives scope, period or auditor. Treat as unverified vendor marketing.

claim_as_stated: NPT FY2025 annual report: 159,543 grants processed (+23% YoY), $6.44b granted
exact_values_found: "NPT granted $6.44 billion on behalf of donors in FY25, a 17% increase"; "159,543 grants were processed, a 23% increase year over year". Form 990 TY2024 (FYE 6/2025) line 13 grants paid $6,415,072,479.
discrepancies: None vs annual report. About $25m gap between annual report and 990 grants paid.
interpretation_challenge: Annual report may be family-wide (incl. affiliates) vs 990 single EIN; processed grant count is not paid/settled count.

claim_as_stated: Fidelity Charitable audited statements (Note 7) document a contractual administrative-fee payment formula to FMR (Fidelity affiliate); ~$84.3m investment management fees
exact_values_found: Note 7: "the Gift Fund paid FMR at amounts equal to the administrative fee the Gift Fund charged its donors, net of any tier price credits". Statement of activities FY2025: administrative fees $179,875,837; investment management fees $84,317,489 (FY2024 $67,308,635). Admin fee .60% with tier credits ($29,133,496 at 6/30/2025).
discrepancies: None material. Internal cross-reference in Note 2 says "see Note 8" for service provider; content is in Note 7.
interpretation_challenge: Note 7 ties administrative fees (not the $84.3m investment management fees) to FMR. Do not attribute all $84.3m to FMR.

claim_as_stated: Vanguard Charitable Note 1 documents $4.014m related-party support fees and 35 of 37 pools are affiliated Vanguard funds
exact_values_found: Note 1: "thirty-seven investment pools ... Thirty-five pools are comprised of mutual funds and exchange traded funds offered by The Vanguard Group, Inc. (Vanguard), a related party"; support-service fees "for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were $4,243,096 and $4,014,052". In-kind services from Vanguard $1,195,752 (FY26), $1,000,342 (FY25).
discrepancies: $4.014m is FY2025 (FYE 6/30/2025); the current FY2026 figure is $4,243,096. Claim omits fiscal year and is now superseded. Source wording: "certain support services including investment recordkeeping and administrative services".
interpretation_challenge: A count of pools is not asset weighting; affiliated fund expense ratios and in-kind services are separate economics.

(Impact Fund) owns a portion of an entity that in turn owns a portion of Foundation Source." "CharityVest utilizes Foundation Source ... for certain technological and operations assistance."
